title: Requests, Limits, Quotas and LimitRange

header.html: Understand requests, limits, quotas; Define resource requirements

toc.title: LimitRange: defaults and bounds per container

html:
1Requests and limits

Every container can declare how much CPU and memory it needs:

resources:
  requests: {cpu: 100m, memory: 64Mi}    # what it asks for: used to choose a node
  limits:   {cpu: 200m, memory: 128Mi}   # the most it may use: enforced while running
Request Limit
Who uses it the scheduler: a Pod goes only to a node with enough unreserved capacity the kubelet and the container runtime
CPU over the value n/a the container is throttled (slowed), not killed
Memory over the value n/a the container is killed (OOMKilled, exit code 137) and restarted
If missing treated as 0 (or the LimitRange default) no limit (or the LimitRange default); if only a limit is set, the request equals it

Units. CPU: 1 is one core, 500m is half a core (milli-CPU). Memory: bytes with suffixes Ki, Mi, Gi (powers of 1024) or K, M, G (powers of 1000). 128Mi and 128M are different.

k run sized --image=nginx:alpine --dry-run=client -o yaml > pod.yaml   # then add resources: under the container and apply (kubectl run has no --requests or --limits flag)
k set resources deployment hog --requests=memory=64Mi --limits=memory=256Mi
k describe node <node> | grep -A8 "Allocated resources"

A Pod whose requests do not fit on any node stays Pending with "0/3 nodes are available: ... Insufficient cpu". Fix it by lowering the request (a bare Pod must be recreated; a Deployment is edited) or by freeing capacity.

2Quality of Service classes

Kubernetes puts each Pod into a QoS class from its requests and limits. The class decides who is evicted first when a node runs out of memory.

Class Rule Eviction order
Guaranteed every container has requests equal to limits for both CPU and memory last
Burstable at least one request or limit set, but not Guaranteed middle
BestEffort no requests and no limits at all first

Read it with k get pod <pod> -o jsonpath='{.status.qosClass}'.

3ResourceQuota: a budget per namespace

A ResourceQuota caps what a whole namespace may use. It is how an administrator shares a cluster between teams.

k create quota team-quota --hard=pods=3,requests.cpu=500m,limits.memory=1Gi -n quota
k describe quota team-quota -n quota     # Used and Hard side by side
Quota key Limits
pods, services, configmaps, secrets, persistentvolumeclaims the count of objects
requests.cpu, requests.memory the sum of requests of all Pods
limits.cpu, limits.memory the sum of limits of all Pods
requests.storage the sum of PVC sizes

Two consequences you must know:

  1. When a quota covers CPU or memory (requests.* or limits.*), every new Pod must declare that request or limit, or the API server rejects it: must specify limits.memory. Add the values, or create a LimitRange that supplies defaults.
  2. When a quota is full, the Deployment is accepted but its ReplicaSet cannot create the Pods: get deploy shows 2/4, and the cause is in k get events or k describe rs: forbidden: exceeded quota. Raise the quota or lower the usage.

4LimitRange: defaults and bounds per container

A LimitRange works inside a namespace on each container or Pod: it fills in defaults and rejects values outside min and max.

apiVersion: v1
kind: LimitRange
metadata: {name: defaults}
spec:
  limits:
  - type: Container
    default:        {cpu: 200m, memory: 128Mi}    # limit when none is given
    defaultRequest: {cpu: 100m, memory: 64Mi}     # request when none is given
    max: {cpu: 500m}                              # nothing above this is accepted
    min: {cpu: 50m}

The defaults apply when a Pod is created: existing Pods are not changed. A Pod that asks for more than max is rejected with maximum cpu usage per Container is 500m, but limit is 1. Quotas and LimitRanges are checked by admission control when the object is created (Module 11), not while the Pod runs.

ResourceQuota LimitRange
Scope the whole namespace (sum) one container, Pod or PVC
Does caps totals and counts sets defaults, min and max
Needs the Pod to declare resources yes (for the covered resources) no: it can supply them

5When the limit is hit

What you see Meaning Fix
OOMKilled, exit code 137, restarts memory use above the limit raise the memory limit (and request) or fix the leak
App slow, CPU at its limit in k top CPU throttling raise the CPU limit
Pending, Insufficient cpu/memory the request does not fit any node lower the request
forbidden: exceeded quota the namespace budget is spent raise the quota or remove objects
must specify limits.memory quota requires it add resources or a LimitRange default
Exam tip

. In "set the resources of this Deployment" tasks use k set resources deployment <name> --requests=... --limits=...: one command, and it triggers the rollout for you.

Exam tip

. k describe quota shows Used and Hard: read it before you change anything. Do not delete a quota to "fix" a task unless the task says so.

6Lab tasks

<!-- LABS: m10 -->

Lab 10.1: requests limits qos

Domain: Environment | Points: 6 | Time: about 6 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m10-01-requests-limits-qos)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

In the namespace res, create a Pod named sized (image nginx:alpine) whose container requests 100m CPU and 64Mi memory and is limited to 200m CPU and 128Mi memory. Wait until it is Running. Then write the Pod's QoS class (just the class name) to ~/answers/qos.txt on the host where you run kubectl.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n res run sized --image=nginx:alpine --dry-run=client -o yaml > /tmp/sized.yaml
sed -i 's/^    resources: {}/    resources:\n      requests: {cpu: 100m, memory: 64Mi}\n      limits: {cpu: 200m, memory: 128Mi}/' /tmp/sized.yaml
kubectl apply -f /tmp/sized.yaml
kubectl -n res wait --for=condition=Ready pod/sized --timeout=120s
kubectl -n res get pod sized -o jsonpath='{.status.qosClass}' > ~/answers/qos.txt
cat ~/answers/qos.txt

Lab 10.2: oomkilled limit

Domain: Environment | Points: 7 | Time: about 8 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m10-02-oomkilled-limit)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

In the namespace res, the Pod of the Deployment hog is repeatedly killed because it uses more memory than its limit (OOMKilled). Without changing the image or the command, set the memory limit of its container to 256Mi and its memory request to 64Mi, and wait until the Deployment has 1 Ready replica that keeps running.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n res describe pod -l app=hog | grep -iE "OOMKilled|Reason|Limits|memory"
kubectl -n res set resources deployment hog --requests=memory=64Mi --limits=memory=256Mi
kubectl -n res rollout status deployment hog --timeout=120s

Lab 10.3: resource quota

Domain: Environment | Points: 7 | Time: about 7 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m10-03-resource-quota)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

In the namespace quota, create a ResourceQuota named team-quota that allows at most 3 Pods, 500m of total CPU requests and 1Gi of total memory limits. Then create a Deployment web (image nginx:alpine, 2 replicas) whose Pods each request 100m CPU and have a memory limit of 256Mi, so that both replicas are Ready within the quota.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n quota create quota team-quota --hard=pods=3,requests.cpu=500m,limits.memory=1Gi
kubectl -n quota create deployment web --image=nginx:alpine --replicas=2 --dry-run=client -o yaml > /tmp/web.yaml
sed -i 's/^        resources: {}/        resources:\n          requests: {cpu: 100m}\n          limits: {memory: 256Mi}/' /tmp/web.yaml
kubectl apply -f /tmp/web.yaml
kubectl -n quota rollout status deployment web --timeout=120s
kubectl -n quota describe quota team-quota

Lab 10.4: quota exceeded

Domain: Environment | Points: 6 | Time: about 6 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m10-04-quota-exceeded)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

In the namespace quota, the Deployment batch should run 4 replicas, but only 2 Pods exist: the events show that the Pods exceed the ResourceQuota limits-pods. Do not change the Deployment: raise the quota so that it allows 4 Pods, and wait until all 4 replicas are Ready.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n quota describe quota limits-pods
kubectl -n quota get events --sort-by=.lastTimestamp | tail -3
kubectl -n quota patch quota limits-pods -p '{"spec":{"hard":{"pods":"4"}}}'
kubectl -n quota rollout status deployment batch --timeout=120s

Lab 10.5: limitrange defaults

Domain: Environment | Points: 7 | Time: about 7 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m10-05-limitrange-defaults)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

In the namespace lr, create a LimitRange named defaults for containers: default limits 200m CPU and 128Mi memory, default requests 100m CPU and 64Mi memory, and a maximum of 500m CPU per container. Then create a Pod plain (image nginx:alpine) without any resources, and confirm that it received the defaults. A Pod that asks for 1 CPU must be rejected in this namespace.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n lr apply -f - <<'Y'
apiVersion: v1
kind: LimitRange
metadata: {name: defaults}
spec:
  limits:
  - type: Container
    default: {cpu: 200m, memory: 128Mi}
    defaultRequest: {cpu: 100m, memory: 64Mi}
    max: {cpu: 500m}
Y
kubectl -n lr run plain --image=nginx:alpine
kubectl -n lr wait --for=condition=Ready pod/plain --timeout=120s
kubectl -n lr get pod plain -o jsonpath='{.spec.containers[0].resources}'; echo
kubectl -n lr apply -f - <<'Y' || echo "rejected as expected"
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata: {name: toobig}
spec:
  containers:
  - name: main
    image: nginx:alpine
    resources:
      limits: {cpu: "1"}
Y

Lab 10.6: qos classes

Domain: Environment | Points: 5 | Time: about 5 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m10-06-qos-classes)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

In the namespace res, three Pods exist: q1, q2 and q3. Write one line per Pod to ~/answers/qos.txt in the form <pod> <QoS class>, sorted by Pod name, using the class that Kubernetes assigned (read it from the cluster).

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

for p in q1 q2 q3; do echo "$p $(kubectl -n res get pod $p -o jsonpath='{.status.qosClass}')"; done | sort > ~/answers/qos.txt
cat ~/answers/qos.txt

<!-- /LABS -->

7Recall questions

R1Who uses the resource request, and who enforces the limit?

Show the answer

The scheduler uses requests to place Pods; the kubelet and runtime enforce limits.

R2What happens when a container exceeds its CPU limit? Its memory limit?

Show the answer

CPU: it is throttled. Memory: it is killed (OOMKilled) and restarted.

R3What are the three QoS classes?

Show the answer

Guaranteed, Burstable and BestEffort.

R4When is a Pod Guaranteed?

Show the answer

When every container has CPU and memory requests equal to its limits.

R5What does a ResourceQuota limit?

Show the answer

The total resources and object counts of a namespace.

R6Why can a Deployment show 2/4 Pods when the namespace has a full quota?

Show the answer

The ReplicaSet cannot create more Pods: exceeded quota.

R7What does a LimitRange do?

Show the answer

It sets default requests and limits and enforces min and max for containers in a namespace.

R8What is the difference between 128Mi and 128M?

Show the answer

Mi is 1024-based (mebibytes), M is 1000-based (megabytes).

Quick Reference Card

Topic Remember
Request scheduling input; Pending if no node fits
Limit CPU throttled, memory OOMKilled (137)
Units 100m CPU, 64Mi memory
QoS Guaranteed (requests = limits), Burstable, BestEffort
ResourceQuota namespace totals and counts; describe quota
LimitRange defaults, min, max per container; applied at creation
Commands set resources (Deployments), YAML resources: (Pods), create quota --hard
Quota effects Pods must declare resources; full quota blocks the ReplicaSet
